main_body: Corrugated slate-metal roof slope (rows ~47-91) over a brick front wall with arched windows, a riveted iron door and copper pipes (rows 92-126), plus a brick chimney.
top_band: Roof slope, read at x=80: light L=158 at row 49 and rows 59-63, then L=122 across rows 64-81, darkening to L=95 at rows 82-90. A dark skylight vent sits at rows 53-58. The slope ends at an orange eave line (rows 92-93).
evidence: The roof is a large sloped surface with a trapezoid silhouette and a skylight band, like the reference house roofs. It is separated from the wall by an orange eave line at rows 92-93 and a dark shadow row at 94. The wall below has inset arched windows and a recessed iron door. Both the top surface and the front face are clearly drawn, and no receding side face is shown.

style.evidence: The roof has about 4-5 slate steps, vertical corrugation lines and rust specks, and the brick wall and lit windows have some detail. Against the references the piece is thinner: 37 distinct colours versus 66 and 185, and a median of 9 colours per tile versus 11 and 18. Dark edge pixels are 89% near-neutral (references 7-9%), so the roof outline reads as a near-black sticker line, even though the wall outline is tinted. The material ramps and outline craft sit below the Beodeul standard, so it fails.
